title: Scoped public command execution
description: The public command contract consumed by a user or skill-guided participant: explicit requests yield actual bounded observations and side-effect outcomes without conferring engineering decisions.

operations.name: execute_public_request
operations.purpose: Execute one admitted public command within its declared command-family scope.
inputs: Supported command family, version domain, explicit selectors and actor-supplied arguments or request.
Applicable project context and authority for any requested side effect.
outputs: The command family's declared human or structured result, exit outcome, diagnostics, omitted-detail access where applicable, and accurate mutation or no-mutation disposition.
behavior: Reject unknown commands, unsupported versions, malformed selectors, and invalid modes under the family-specific early-error contract.
Dispatch record operations through IF-003 and installation through IF-006 while preserving each operation's exact allowed effects.
Keep recorded values separate from observations and bounded advice. Preserve conflict, unchanged, failed, partial, and committed outcomes rather than converting them to workflow judgments.
Protect private diagnostic content and provide the supported route to materially omitted detail; output bounds cannot hide failures or make a valid correction unrecordable.
Permit standalone skills to avoid command use; governed recording uses an explicit supported request, not implicit installation or inferred state changes.

Honor each family's help/version and invalid-input ordering before repository or stdin access where required, including independent early-error response versions. Omit unavailable identities instead of inventing a validated stored contract.

Perform discovery as bounded factual observation and record queries as literal actor selection. Never auto-select a sole candidate, hide malformed current residue as retired history, or broaden selection from a skill label.

Preserve full versus selected content, optional absence, deliberate omissions, count scope, and separate selection/observation-detail continuation identities. Serialize complete bounded human or machine output before emitting it; do not silently truncate narrative or create a nonprogressing page.

For mutations, use IF-003's fresh execution under writer exclusion, obtain its exact guarded candidate and bounded storage facts, and serialize the mandatory public receipt before replacement. Establish readiness applicable to that same operation/candidate/format; preserve the published bound with optional diagnostic omission rather than rejecting an admissible correction. No preview is an executable transaction, and no new wire token or callback mechanism is implied.

Preview preserves the intended candidate and bounded result while remaining non-writing and non-reserving. Recovery uses explicit transaction identity and complete/restore selection; retries never invent renewed decision basis or replay an old mutation implicitly.

Keep private invocation diagnostics bounded and independent of semantic results, stdout, authoritative repository bytes, and transaction/recovery behavior. Validate closed logging options at the declared admission boundary, protect owned paths and sensitive input, and expose exact-ID lookup as read-only diagnosis rather than command replay or workflow evidence.

failure_behavior.condition: The requested operation is unknown, unsupported, malformed, or outside its admitted scope.
failure_behavior.outcome: Return the applicable family-specific error without downstream side effects; do not guess a corrected request.

failure_behavior.condition: The selected operation reports conflict, incomplete effects, failed access, or required recovery.
failure_behavior.outcome: Preserve that actual result and its safe next decision boundary without asserting successful progression or silently repeating a mutation.

consistency_rules: The command result must reflect actual effects. A completed write cannot be reported as an unperformed plan or a rejected operation because optional reporting was incomplete.
Scope and authority remain attributable to the supplied request; a skill, role label, or successful command is not a new authorization.
Human and machine-facing outcomes retain the owning command family's distinctions and exit behavior.

Public result domains remain independent of stored v3 and of generic/discovery/advanced interfaces. In particular, unsupported or unavailable stored content cannot justify a fabricated validated revision or a guessed response version.
compatibility_rules: The current CLI Design owns literal names, flags, envelopes, output contracts, and supported versions. This Interface does not create another RPC or network protocol.
Skill-guided consumers must use supported command contracts and cannot assume new REM model operations exist.
Public contract changes must reconcile all invoking skill guidance, examples, and affected consumers before adoption.

The proposed browser-v1 request/result family is defined by MOD-010 and IF-012; it is not a v2 operational-record command or an observed public entry. Existing command/record behavior remains version-scoped until coordinated adoption.

sources.basis: Connect common guided invocation to the public command responsibility without weakening CLI ownership or making every skill depend on CLI; see SRC-PUBLISHED-CLI and SRC-PUBLISHED-SKILLS.

Reconcile IR-008 acceptance outcomes and its allocated obligations with explicit command/persistence cooperation, preserving existing CLI/Record Format authority and external-edit limits. The refinement supplies no new executable or public wire format.

Apply refined REM Architecture Design through subordinate observed and proposed views. Preserve the logical allocation, existing public contracts, and draft status; source mapping is not executed satisfaction evidence.

The existing public command contract and local process binding serve external users and agents. Expose the same contract through Engineering operations; MOD-010 remains the sole provider and MOD-012 remains its declared Module consumer.

Refine contract accountability: MOD-018 provides IF-004 and MOD-019 provides IF-006. MOD-010 and MOD-014 retain their behavioral allocations and state responsibilities. This supersedes the provider/exposure choice recorded by SRC-MODULE-HIERARCHY without changing Interface guarantees, consumers, Function/AR allocations, or realization observations. Earlier source entries retain their prior design meaning; this draft refinement supplies no runtime adoption or satisfaction evidence.

System and Architecture Design from SR-084–088 and refined SR-060; proposed responsibility, contract and realization only. No implementation, platform qualification or product availability is established.
